questions.prompt: Three web apps share one Standard App Service plan with two instances. One app consumes most of the CPU and slows the others. What isolates its compute?
options: Scale the plan out to four instances
Create a deployment slot for the busy app
Move the busy app to its own App Service plan
Enable VNet integration on the busy app
questions.explanation: Compute is dedicated at the plan level, not per app. Isolating an app's compute means a separate plan.
why_not: All apps in a plan run on all its instances; scaling out still shares them.
Slots run in the same plan and share its instances.
Integration affects outbound networking, not compute sharing.
questions.clue: "share one plan" and one app "slows the others": apps on a plan share its instances.

questions.prompt: What is the lowest App Service tier that supports a custom domain with a TLS (SNI) binding?
options: Free
Basic
Shared
Standard
questions.explanation: Custom TLS bindings require the Basic, Standard, Premium or Isolated tiers; F1 and D1 don't support them.
why_not: Free doesn't support TLS bindings.
Shared doesn't support TLS bindings either.
Standard supports it, but Basic is the lowest tier that does.
questions.clue: "lowest tier" for a custom domain with an SNI binding: Basic.

questions.sub_skill: Configure scaling for an App Service plan
questions.prompt: A web app must add instances automatically when CPU exceeds 70%, using rules. What is the minimum tier?
options: Standard
Basic
Free
Premium v3
questions.explanation: Rule-based autoscale on an App Service plan requires Standard or higher; Basic scales out manually.
why_not: Basic supports manual scale-out only.
Free has no dedicated instances to scale.
Premium v3 supports it, but Standard is the minimum for rule-based autoscale.
questions.clue: "automatically" and "using rules": rule-based autoscale starts at Standard.

questions.sub_skill: Configure scaling for an App Service plan
questions.prompt: An app in a Premium v3 plan must scale with incoming HTTP traffic without anyone writing autoscale rules, up to 20 instances. What should you enable?
options: Rule-based autoscale with a CPU rule
Scale up to Isolated v2
Manual scale out to 20 instances
Automatic scaling, with a maximum burst of 20
questions.explanation: Automatic scaling (Premium v2, v3, v4) scales on HTTP load with a maximum burst, with no rules to configure.
why_not: That needs rules, which the requirement rules out.
Isolation changes the environment, not how scaling is triggered.
That runs 20 instances all the time instead of scaling with traffic.
questions.clue: "Premium v3" and "without anyone writing autoscale rules": automatic scaling.

questions.prompt: You need to move a web app to another App Service plan. Which conditions must hold?
options: Any plan in the same subscription
The plans are in the same resource group, region and operating system
The target plan must be in a higher tier
The app must first be stopped and backed up
questions.explanation: An app can move to a plan in the same resource group, region and OS as its current plan.
why_not: Plans in other resource groups or regions don't qualify.
Tier isn't the constraint; location, resource group and OS are.
Neither is required for the move.
questions.clue: "move a web app to another plan": same resource group, region and operating system.

questions.prompt: A web app named contoso-shop is created in an App Service plan in West Europe. What is its default URL, and where does it run?
options: https://contoso-shop.azurewebsites.net, on the plan's instances in West Europe
https://contoso-shop.westeurope.cloudapp.net, on a VM you manage
https://contoso-shop.azurewebsites.net, in any region Azure chooses
A private URL only, until a custom domain is added
questions.explanation: An app takes its plan's region and instances, and gets a default <name>.azurewebsites.net host name.
why_not: App Service apps use azurewebsites.net and run on the plan's managed instances.
An app runs in its plan's region.
Every app gets a public azurewebsites.net name by default.
questions.clue: "default URL" for contoso-shop: <name>.azurewebsites.net, running on the plan's instances.

questions.sub_skill: Configure certificates and Transport Layer Security (TLS) for an App Service
questions.prompt: You need a free certificate for www.contoso.com that App Service renews automatically. Which option, and what can't it do?
options: An App Service certificate; it can't be renewed
A Key Vault certificate; it can't be bound with SNI
A self-signed upload; it can't be used for HTTPS
An App Service managed certificate; it can't be a wildcard or be exported
questions.explanation: App Service managed certificates are free and auto-renewed, but they don't support wildcards and aren't exportable.
why_not: App Service certificates are paid and do renew; they support wildcards.
Key Vault certificates can be bound with SNI, and they aren't free.
A self-signed PFX can be bound, but it isn't free-and-managed or trusted by browsers.
questions.clue: "free" and "renews automatically": an App Service managed certificate, which has limits.

questions.sub_skill: Configure certificates and Transport Layer Security (TLS) for an App Service
questions.prompt: An app must keep using TLS for an old client that doesn't support SNI. What binding, and what is the impact?
options: An SNI binding in Basic, which is free
HTTPS Only on the Free tier
An IP-based SSL binding, which needs Standard or higher and bills hourly
A minimum TLS version of 1.0
questions.explanation: IP-based SSL gives the app a dedicated address for clients without SNI. It requires Standard or higher and carries an hourly charge.
why_not: SNI requires the client to support SNI.
HTTPS Only doesn't change the binding type, and Free has no TLS bindings.
The TLS version isn't the issue; SNI support is.
questions.clue: "doesn't support SNI": an IP-based binding, which costs more and needs Standard or higher.

questions.sub_skill: Map an existing custom DNS name to an App Service
questions.prompt: You're mapping the root domain contoso.com to a web app. Which DNS records do you create?
options: An A record for @ pointing to the app's IP, and a TXT record asuid with the domain verification ID
A CNAME for @ pointing to the app's azurewebsites.net name
A CNAME and an A record for @, for redundancy
Only a TXT record asuid
questions.explanation: A root domain needs an A record (@) pointing at the app's IP plus a TXT asuid record holding the verification ID.
why_not: Root domains use an A record in the documented procedure.
Never configure both for the same name; they conflict.
The TXT record verifies ownership; a mapping record is still required.
questions.clue: "root domain": a CNAME can't sit at the apex, so an A record plus the asuid TXT record.

questions.sub_skill: Map an existing custom DNS name to an App Service
questions.prompt: Why does Microsoft strongly recommend the TXT asuid record when mapping a custom domain?
options: It enables HTTPS automatically
It verifies domain ownership and helps prevent subdomain takeover by other App Service apps
It makes the domain resolve faster
It's required for IP-based SSL only
questions.explanation: The domain verification ID in the asuid TXT record helps avoid subdomain takeovers from other App Service apps.
why_not: HTTPS needs a certificate binding.
The TXT record doesn't affect resolution of the app's name.
It applies to every custom domain mapping.
questions.clue: "strongly recommend the TXT asuid record": it proves ownership and prevents subdomain takeover.

questions.sub_skill: Configure backup for an App Service
questions.prompt: You need backups every 4 hours, kept for 90 days, that you can download. What should you configure?
options: Automatic backups
Custom backups with a 90-day retention setting
Custom backups to a storage account, with retention set to indefinite and old backups removed by your own process
Azure Backup for the App Service plan
questions.explanation: Custom backups go to a storage account, run on a schedule (every 2 hours at the most), are downloadable, and retain 0-30 days or indefinitely.
why_not: They're hourly, kept 30 days, can't be configured and can't be downloaded.
Custom retention is 0-30 days or indefinite; 90 isn't an option.
App Service backup is configured on the app, not as a plan-level Azure Backup item.
questions.clue: "every 4 hours", "90 days" and "download": custom backups to your own storage account.

questions.sub_skill: Configure backup for an App Service
questions.prompt: After restoring a web app from a backup into a new app, users can't reach it at its custom domain over HTTPS. Why?
options: The backup didn't include the site content
Restores always fail for Standard tier
The app must be restored to a slot first
Custom domains and TLS bindings aren't restored; they must be re-applied
questions.explanation: Restore brings back content and app configuration but not custom domains, TLS/SSL, managed identities or networking features.
why_not: Content is included in backups.
Restores are supported in Basic and higher.
Restoring to a new app is supported.
questions.clue: "restoring into a new app" and HTTPS on the custom domain fails: domains and bindings aren't restored.

questions.sub_skill: Configure networking settings for an App Service
questions.prompt: A web app has one access restriction rule: Allow 203.0.113.0/24, priority 100. No unmatched action has been set. A request arrives from 198.51.100.7. What happens?
options: It's denied with 403, because adding a rule makes unmatched traffic denied
It's allowed, because the default is allow
It's allowed, but logged
It's redirected to the scm site
questions.explanation: With no rules, everything is allowed; once one rule exists, unmatched requests are implicitly denied (HTTP 403).
why_not: The default is allow only while there are no rules.
Access restrictions don't have an allow-and-log mode.
Rules don't redirect.
questions.clue: "one Allow rule" and "no unmatched action set": adding a rule makes unmatched traffic denied.

questions.sub_skill: Configure networking settings for an App Service
questions.prompt: A web app must call a SQL database that's reachable only inside a virtual network in the same region. The app itself can stay public. What should you configure?
options: A private endpoint for the app
Virtual network integration, which is outbound
An access restriction allowing the VNet
IP-based SSL
questions.explanation: VNet integration lets the app make outbound calls to resources in the virtual network (Basic tier or higher).
why_not: That makes the app reachable privately inbound; it doesn't let the app call into the VNet.
Access restrictions filter inbound requests to the app.
That's a TLS binding type, not network access.
questions.clue: "call" a resource "inside a virtual network" and "the app can stay public": outbound VNet integration.

questions.sub_skill: Configure deployment slots for an App Service
questions.prompt: Before a swap, staging has FEATURE_X=on (not sticky) and DB=staging-db (sticky). Production has FEATURE_X=off and DB=prod-db (sticky). What does production have after swapping staging into production?
options: FEATURE_X=off and DB=staging-db
FEATURE_X=on and DB=staging-db
FEATURE_X=on and DB=prod-db
FEATURE_X=off and DB=prod-db
questions.explanation: Settings marked as deployment slot settings stay with the slot; others move with the swapped app.
why_not: Non-sticky settings travel with the app, and sticky settings stay with their slot.
DB is a deployment slot setting, so production keeps prod-db.
FEATURE_X isn't sticky, so staging's value moves into production.
questions.clue: "sticky" settings stay with their slot; non-sticky settings move with the swap.

questions.sub_skill: Configure deployment slots for an App Service
questions.prompt: You must test staging with production's settings before production traffic moves, and be able to cancel. Which operation?
options: A regular swap, then swap back if needed
Swap with preview, then complete or cancel the swap
Auto swap
Route 100% of traffic to staging
questions.explanation: Swap with preview applies the target's slot settings to the source and pauses, so you can validate, then complete or cancel.
why_not: That moves traffic immediately; there's no validation pause.
Auto swap swaps after each deployment without a pause.
Traffic routing doesn't apply production's slot settings to staging.
questions.clue: "test staging with production's settings" and "be able to cancel": swap with preview.
